title: Rehoboth Beach Museum

services.name: Boardwalk Walking Tour
services.desc: The Rehoboth Beach Historical Society continues to offer its Ocean Block/Boardwalk walking tours this season, twice a month on Thursdays starting from the bandstand on Rehoboth Avenue at 9am. The tour is a gentle 90minute stroll around town highlighting the history and pointing out important landmarks all while showing pictures from different time periods. Topics include native peoples, the Methodist Camp Meetings, fires, WWII, shipwrecks, storms and more. Parking passes for the tour will be provided when meters are operating. services.name: Historic Rehoboth Beach Bike Tour
services.desc: Pedal through more than a century of Rehoboth Beach history on this guided two-hour bicycle tour led by local historians Patricia and Roger Truitt. Beginning at the Anna Hazzard Tent House, one of the last surviving structures from Rehoboth’s Methodist camp-meeting era, riders are welcomed by “Reverend Todd,” a beloved living-history character who sets the stage for a journey through the landscapes, waterways, and stories that shaped this storied seaside city. From the Tent House, the tour makes its way to Silver Lake, where the Truitts share the history of the Nanticoke people, the first inhabitants of this coastal landscape. services.name: Past Exhibitions
services.desc: Welcome to the Rehoboth Beach Museum's online collections portal. Here you can explore a curated selection of historic photographs, postcards, archives, and artifacts, that document the story of Rehoboth Beach and the surrounding area. These digitized materials offer a glimpse into our community's past-from early seaside Camp Meetings, summer vacations and local businesses, to the people and events that shaped the character of this cherished coastal destination. We invite you to browse, discover, and connect with the history of Rehoboth Beach through these publicly available resources.
